deities: Devi Vaishnavy (Bhagavathy, form of Goddess Durga/Bhadrakali; eight-armed wooden idol, usually veiled behind a golden covering)
festivals: Thrissur Pooram (Medam, April-May; grand rival processions with Thiruvambady, 15 caparisoned elephants from Paramekkavu to Vadakkunnathan temple, Ilanjithara Melam, Kudamattom and fireworks)
Navaratri (nine nights of special poojas, devotional singing and cultural programmes)

history.dynasty: None (temple tradition; associated with the Cochin royal era)
history.period: Ancient (temple tradition; claimed to be over 1,000 years old)
history.summary: The Paramekkavu Bhagavathi Temple, one of the largest Bhagavathy temples in Kerala, stands just outside the Vadakkunnathan temple ground at Paramekkavu, Thrissur. Its presiding deity is Devi Vaishnavy, an incarnation of Goddess Durga worshipped as Bhagavathy in the wooden daru-silpa idol with a unique posture (right leg in padmasana, left leg hanging); the original idol was replaced with a new wooden one on 15 June 1997, and the idol is normally veiled behind a golden covering, revealed only during the Chandatta ritual in Karkidakam (July-August). Legend says a devotee, Appattukuruppal, brought the deity from the Thirumandhamkunnu temple at Angadipuram in his ola kuda (palm-leaf umbrella) when old age kept him from the original temple; the deity rested at the Ilanji thara in the Vadakkunnathan temple before its chaitanya (divinity) was transferred to the present site under a Paro tree - the Parokkavu that became Paramekkavu. The temple is one of the two principal participants in the Thrissur Pooram, the festival of festivals instituted by Sakthan Thampuran of Cochin, standing in friendly rivalry with the Thiruvambady temple.

name: Paramekkavu Bhagavathi Temple
town_description: Thrissur, in central Kerala, is the cultural capital of the state - home to the Vadakkunnathan temple, the Kerala Kalamandalam, and the famed Thrissur Pooram, the grandest temple festival of Kerala. It is well connected by rail and road and lies about 80 km from Kochi, serving as the gateway to the region's celebrated temple circuit.

travel.airport: Cochin International Airport, Nedumbassery (approx. 52-58 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Thrissur Railway Station (approx. 2 km), well connected across India.
travel.road: The temple is at Round East, Thrissur, just outside the Vadakkunnathan temple ground; city buses, autos and taxis ply regularly from the KSRTC stand and railway station.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Thrissur Pooram (April-May) is the grandest but most crowded time; the temple is otherwise serene on weekday mornings.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 4:00 AM to 11:30 AM; evening 4:00 PM to 8:15 PM, open all days (verify - some travel guides list 4:30 AM opening and closing at 9:00 PM). Men must wear dhoti/mundu; photography is restricted inside the sanctum.
